Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: Bank Al‑Maghrib directly manages and administers the Moroccan Gross Settlement System (SRBM/RTGS) as stated on its SRBM page (“managed and administered by Bank Al‑Maghrib”). ([Bank Al‑Maghrib SRBM](https://www.bkam.ma/en/Systems-and-means-of-payment/Financial-markets-infrastructure-and-monitoring/Moroccan-gross-settlement-system-srbm)) Bank Al‑Maghrib also sets up and oversees national retail payment architecture (SIMT) in consultation with banks and supervises payment systems per Article 10 of Law 76‑03. ([Bank Al‑Maghrib payment systems overview](https://www.bkam.ma/en/Systems-and-means-of-payment/Financial-markets-infrastructure-and-monitoring/Overview);[Bank Al‑Maghrib SIMT](https://www.bkam.ma/en/Systems-and-means-of-payment/Financial-markets-infrastructure-and-monitoring/Moroccan-interbank-remote-clearing))
revision_notes: Fetched all three cited Bank Al-Maghrib pages and confirmed they support the score directly: the SRBM page states the system is 'managed and administered by Bank Al-Maghrib', the Overview page confirms SRBM is the large-value system managed by the central bank while retail systems (SIMT, e-money switches) operate under its statutory oversight (Article 10, Law 76-03), and the SIMT page confirms GSIMT operates retail clearing subject to Bank Al-Maghrib's approval of its CEO and governance. Score of 5 (Direct Operation) is well supported by the central bank's own authoritative pages and is confirmed unchanged. As 5 is the maximum code on this scale, flagged for human review per policy despite the clear and current supporting evidence.
revised_comments: Bank Al-Maghrib directly manages and administers Morocco's Gross Settlement System (SRBM) for large-value transfers, as stated on its own regulatory pages. For retail payments, the central bank set up the national reference payment architecture (SIMT) and retains statutory oversight of all payment and clearing systems under Article 10 of Law No. 76-03, with the Groupement pour un Systeme Interbancaire Marocain de Telecompensation (GSIMT) operating SIMT subject to Bank Al-Maghrib's approval of its governance and CEO appointment. This combination of direct operation of the RTGS and close supervisory control of retail infrastructure reflects a governance model in which the central bank goes well beyond a purely regulatory role.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Morocco’s main data protection law (Law 09‑08) does not impose a general mandatory breach notification obligation (no requirement to report security breaches), per Legal 500’s Morocco privacy/cyber guide; breach reporting is only required for entities in “sectors of vital importance” under cybersecurity Law 05‑20. ([Legal 500 Morocco data protection & cyber security guide (PDF)](https://www.legal500.com/guides/wp-content/uploads/sites/1/2022/05/morocco-1.pdf))
revision_notes: The cited Legal 500 (2022) source was fetched and does support the 'no general mandatory breach notification' finding under Law 09-08, but it also flags a carve-out for 'sectors of vital importance' under cybersecurity Law 05-20 that the original score of 1 (No) did not follow through on. Searched further and fetched the text of Law 05-20 (ANRT), its 2021 implementing decree (Decret 2-21-406, Bulletin Officiel), a 2026 regulatory summary (regulations.ai), the Chambers 2026 Data Protection and Privacy practice guide, and a Lexology update dated September 2025. The decree explicitly designates the banking sector as a 'secteur d'activites d'importance vitale' coordinated by Bank Al-Maghrib, meaning banks operating Morocco's payment infrastructure (SRBM/SIMT) are Organismes d'Importance Vitale required to report significant cybersecurity incidents on sensitive information systems to the national cybersecurity authority (DGSSI/maCERT) immediately, with financial penalties under Article 50 for failure to do so. General consumer/data-subject breach notification under Law 09-08 remains voluntary (CNDP encourages but does not mandate it), per the Chambers 2026 guide and Lexology (September 2025), so the original 'No' correctly described that specific channel but missed the mandatory sector-specific cybersecurity incident reporting regime that applies to banks and payment operators as regulated entities. Recalculated to 3 (Mandatory) to reflect this binding regime, since the variable definition explicitly covers notification of cybersecurity incidents to regulators within specified timeframes, which the OIV regime satisfies. As 3 is the top of this scale and the finding rests on combining several sources into a nuanced, sector-specific conclusion, flagged for human review rather than merged automatically.
revised_comments: Morocco has no general legal requirement for mandatory notification of payment data breaches to affected individuals: the National Commission for the Control of Personal Data Protection (CNDP) encourages voluntary breach notification under Law No. 09-08, but this is not compulsory. However, the banking sector, which operates the country's core payment infrastructure (SRBM and SIMT) under Bank Al-Maghrib, is formally classified as a 'secteur d'activites d'importance vitale' under cybersecurity Law No. 05-20 and its 2021 implementing decree. As Organismes d'Importance Vitale, banks and payment operators in this sector must report significant cybersecurity incidents affecting sensitive information systems to the national cybersecurity authority (DGSSI) and its computer emergency response team (maCERT) immediately, with financial penalties for non-compliance under Article 50 of the law. Payment service providers are therefore subject to a mandatory, sector-specific cybersecurity incident notification regime, even though there is no dedicated payment-data breach notification law and no general obligation to notify individual users or the data protection authority directly.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Bank Al‑Maghrib and GSIMT launched the nationwide instant interbank credit transfer service “Virement Instantané” on 1 June 2023, enabling transfers between accounts at different banks in under 20 seconds and available 24/7 (initial cap MAD 20,000). ([Frontier Africa Reports](https://news.frontierafricareports.com/article/morocco-launch-of-instant-interbank-transfer-this-thursday-june-1)) Bank Al‑Maghrib describes Morocco’s payment system architecture with SRBM (RTGS) plus retail systems (SIMT and e‑money switches) forming a national digital payments infrastructure. ([Bank Al‑Maghrib payment systems overview](https://www.bkam.ma/en/Systems-and-means-of-payment/Financial-markets-infrastructure-and-monitoring/Overview))
revision_notes: Original sources (Frontier Africa Reports on the 1 June 2023 launch, and the Bank Al-Maghrib Overview page) were fetched and confirmed as accurate and still valid. Searched for fresher evidence and found two 2025 articles drawing on Bank Al-Maghrib/GSIMT data: Medias24 (29 July 2025) and Hespress (30 November 2025), both citing Bank Al-Maghrib's annual report on payment infrastructure. These show the instant payment system fully operational nationwide with rapidly growing volumes (16.3 million transactions worth around MAD 62 billion in 2024, rising to 14.3 million transactions worth over MAD 52.5 billion by 23 July 2025) and active expansion (payment establishments being onboarded, QR code and Request-to-Pay features in development, a dedicated business offering planned for 2026). Score of 5 (Fully deployed nationwide) is confirmed unchanged and strengthened by this fresher evidence. As 5 is the maximum code on this scale, flagged for human review per policy despite the strong and consistent supporting evidence.
revised_comments: Morocco operates a nationwide instant/real-time interbank transfer service (Virement Instantane), launched by Bank Al-Maghrib and the Groupement pour un Systeme Interbancaire Marocain de Telecompensation (GSIMT) on 1 June 2023. The service settles transfers between accounts at different banks in under 20 seconds, operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and uses the ISO 20022 messaging standard. Adoption has grown rapidly: the system processed 16.3 million transactions worth around MAD 62 billion in 2024, and had already exceeded 14.3 million transactions worth more than MAD 52.5 billion by 23 July 2025, with daily volumes rising from roughly 30,000 in 2023 to around 94,000 in 2025 and a daily record of 286,000 transactions. The service sits alongside Bank Al-Maghrib's Gross Settlement System (SRBM) and other retail infrastructure (SIMT, e-money switches) as part of the national digital payments architecture, and is being extended to licensed payment establishments, with a dedicated business (B2B) offering planned for 2026.
